assessment.nobel_worthiness: Topological insulators opened a new class of quantum matter defined by bulk topology and protected boundary states. The quantum spin Hall proposal and its HgTe realisation are original, conceptually clear and have shaped condensed matter physics, materials science and the search for topological quantum devices. Impact is broad and durable.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the decisive theoretical step (the Z2 classification and the quantum spin Hall proposal), and Molenkamp's group delivered the first experimental demonstration in HgTe wells. Hasan's three-dimensional ARPES work is also major but would need a fourth laureate; the three-name configuration is coherent for the quantum spin Hall line. Other theory groups (e.g. the HgTe prediction) are not in the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Independent confirmations across HgTe, InAs/GaSb, Bi-based three-dimensional materials and photoemission are extensive; the interpretation is stable and the field is mature. Recognition is timely and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Whether the three-dimensional topological insulator experiments (Hasan) should displace Mele or Molenkamp is unresolved.
Proposers of the HgTe quantum-well prediction fall outside the supplied credit.
I cannot independently verify the detailed priority history.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene produced flat bands, correlated insulators and superconductivity in a clean, tunable, carbon-only platform and launched the moire materials field (twistronics). The discovery is original, striking and has led to a large body of follow-on work including fractional Chern insulators.
assessment.attribution: The theory of flat bands at the magic angle (Bistritzer and MacDonald) and the 2018 correlated-insulator and superconductivity experiments (Jarillo-Herrero and collaborators) are clearly decisive; Andrei's earlier STM evidence for van Hove singularities and flat bands in twisted layers is an important complementary observation. Bistritzer's equal role in the theory is a real allocation problem under a three-person limit; the early-career experimental co-authors are also not credited.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed by many independent groups since 2018; some microscopic questions (pairing mechanism) remain open, which does not undermine the discovery. Timing is reasonable, a little early relative to the long-run impact.
uncertainties: Exclusion of Bistritzer from the proposed three is a credit tension.
Pairing mechanism and reproducibility of device-level superconductivity are still debated.
Relative weight of Andrei's STM work versus the transport discovery is a judgment call.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The localisation of gamma-ray burst X-ray afterglows with BeppoSAX and the follow-up optical and radio identification and redshift measurements settled the cosmological origin of GRBs after a three-decade puzzle. This is a clean, high-impact discovery of astrophysics and gamma-ray astronomy with lasting consequences for relativistic-outflow physics, black-hole formation and multi-messenger work.
assessment.attribution: Costa and Frontera led the BeppoSAX Wide Field Camera and narrow-field detection that gave arcminute positions and the first X-ray afterglow; Kulkarni's group provided the decisive optical and radio redshift and energetics work (with others). Credit is shared with the late J. van Paradijs, the Caltech and Carnegie observers, and the large BeppoSAX team, so the three names are defensible but not unique.
assessment.maturity: Overwhelmingly confirmed by Swift, Fermi and thousands of subsequent afterglows; the interpretation is stable. The discovery dates from 1997, so recognition is mature and arguably late.
uncertainties: Allocation among the BeppoSAX instrument team, optical identifiers and the deceased van Paradijs is contested.
Whether the committee regards this as physics rather than astronomy for the purposes of the prize is a judgment call.
Specific detail of the 1997 chronology is from memory and not independently verified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The IceCube detection of a diffuse flux of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos, and the 2018 association of a neutrino with the blazar TXS 0506+056, opened neutrino astronomy and are a major achievement of astroparticle instrumentation, with a cubic-kilometre detector built in the Antarctic ice. Originality is high and the impact on multi-messenger astrophysics is lasting.
assessment.attribution: Halzen is the principal conceptual and scientific driver of IceCube, but the discovery is the work of a collaboration of hundreds, and the supplied credit lists only one name. A fair prize configuration would plausibly also involve early neutrino-telescope pioneers (e.g. DUMAND and AMANDA lineages) and key detector builders, none of whom are credited here. A one-person prize for a collaboration discovery is a weakness.
assessment.maturity: The diffuse flux is established at high significance and supported by independent measurements. Source identification is still partial (TXS and NGC 1068 are evidence-level but at modest significance), so the astrophysical interpretation is still developing. Recognition is somewhat premature on origin but mature on the existence of the flux.
uncertainties: Attribution to a single individual is hard to defend for a large collaboration.
Source population and production mechanisms remain unresolved.
I have a professional familiarity with the astroparticle field and have tried to weigh this candidate by the same standard as the others.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, using the magic-wavelength proposal and its realisation, reached fractional uncertainties near 1e-18 and are now the most precise measurement devices, with applications to redefinition of the second, tests of fundamental constants and relativistic geodesy. The discovery is original, clear and of lasting importance in precision measurement.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength optical lattice scheme and demonstrated the first strontium lattice clock; Ye led the group that pushed systematic uncertainty and coherence to record levels. A two-person configuration is clean, though other groups (e.g. Ytterbium and the NIST and PTB clocks) and the earlier ion-clock work contributed.
assessment.maturity: Independent confirmation is extensive across many laboratories and species, and the technology is operating. The redefinition of the second is still pending, so practical maturity is high but not complete. Timing is reasonable.
uncertainties: Credit relative to the ion-clock and the frequency-comb lineages already recognised is not fully resolved.
Whether the community sees this as an extension of the 2005 prize is a judgment.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The measurement of a non-zero theta13 closed the last unknown mixing angle of three-flavour neutrino oscillations and opened the way to leptonic CP-violation searches and mass-ordering determination. It is a precise, well-defined experimental result with clear importance for particle physics.
assessment.attribution: Daya Bay (Wang, Luk) reported the decisive reactor-antineutrino disappearance at 5 sigma in 2012, and T2K (Nishikawa) reported the first accelerator electron-neutrino appearance indication in 2011. The RENO and Double Chooz teams made essentially simultaneous independent measurements, and the credited names omit them. The attribution is strongly collaboration-based and the allocation is fragile.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by several experiments with consistent values; the interpretation is stable. Timing is mature, but the 2015 prize already recognised neutrino oscillations, so the marginal discovery is arguably less distinctive.
uncertainties: Contested credit among Daya Bay, RENO, Double Chooz and T2K.
Whether a measurement of a mixing parameter has the same standing as the discovery of oscillation itself.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum simulation with ultracold atoms in optical lattices, including the superfluid to Mott-insulator transition and quantum-gas microscopy, created a controllable laboratory for many-body physics. The idea and its realisation are original and have led to a broad programme of Hubbard-model, topological and out-of-equilibrium experiments.
assessment.attribution: The Jaksch-Zoller proposal and the Greiner-Hansch-Bloch Mott experiment are the foundational step, while Bloch's group extended the platform and Greiner developed the quantum gas microscope. Esslinger and Cirac have strong claims too, and five names are credited, so the three-laureate limit forces a difficult exclusion.
assessment.maturity: Highly reproducible and widely implemented; the field is mature, though the long-promised solution of open condensed-matter problems by analog simulation is still partly aspirational. The 2001 and 2012 prizes have already recognised neighbouring work.
uncertainties: Allocation among five strong claimants is unresolved.
The extent to which analog simulators have answered open scientific questions remains partial.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit quantum electrodynamics established the standard architecture for superconducting quantum processors, with strong dispersive coupling of a qubit to a resonator enabling readout and control. It is original, clear and has driven large-scale quantum-computing development.
assessment.attribution: Blais and collaborators proposed the architecture and Wallraff and Schoelkopf with colleagues demonstrated strong coupling in 2004; the credit set is compact and coherent. Devoret, Martinis and Clarke were recognised in 2025 for the underlying macroscopic quantum effects, which narrows the incremental case.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced by numerous laboratories and industrial groups; interpretation is stable. The recent prize on superconducting circuits makes a closely related award less timely.
uncertainties: Overlap with the recently recognised work.
Whether the committee wishes to recognise a quantum-computing architecture as physics discovery rather than engineering.
